manchete.trecho: We know, rumors will be rumors. But when we get wind of as many as we have lately, it’s usually not surprising when many of them end up being true. The type of rumors can also give you a sense of the announcements that might come out. And everything we’re hearing about Canon’s end-of-year slowdown leading to a fast 2027 launch does seem to be lining up. Let’s look at a few rumors swirling online to see what might be in the cards for Canon to announce at the start of the next calendar year, with cameras, lenses, and more possibly on the docket. Canon Rumors Swirling According to reports on Canon Rumors , there appear to be not one or two, but several new cameras and lenses set to be announced by the company soon. noticias.trecho: A large light well brings daylight deep into this private home that was designed by Desai Chia Architecture for a tight site in a dense Maryland neighbourhood. The project takes its name from its location in Bethesda, a city located northwest of Washington DC. The house is set within a suburban neighbourhood near the downtown district, where residential lots are about one-fifth of an acre (647 square metres). Because the houses here are close together, the architects needed to be very mindful of privacy concerns. noticias.trecho: STUDIO MASSIMO EMBEDS TIMBER OFFICE INTO DUTCH HEATHLAND   Situated on the Tafelberg heath in Blaricum, east of Amsterdam , Office by Nature, Tafelberg is a 1,120-sqm timber office designed by Studio Massimo. Built within a protected glacial landscape and drinking-water catchment area, the project required low-impact construction to protect the surrounding soil. Taking structural and formal cues from the regional plaggenhut, a traditional earthen-walled dwelling topped with a sod roof, the building merges directly with the terrain. The ground slopes upward without an edge or material break to form a walkable living roof planted with more than one hundred native, organically grown species.   Each elevation responds to its orientation. noticias.trecho: Movity is a new video hosting and portfolio platform for filmmakers, built by cinematographer and director Arkadiy Kreslov. It combines hosting, client review, and embeds with a search engine that finds films by their key frames, color palette, and dialogue. A curated public feed accepts only verified filmmakers and excludes work made primarily with generative AI. Let’s take a closer look. We’ve written and spoken about Vimeo quite a bit lately. Bending Spoons acquired the platform in late 2025, and in January 2026 we reported that Vimeo layoffs eliminated the majority of staff just four months after the deal. We also looked at how Vimeo betrayed the filmmakers who built it , as well as an opinion piece by my colleague Jeff Loch on how Vimeo is holding him hostage . noticias.titulo: Birds, browser windows and broken connections: inside Gigi Borgese’s drawings
noticias.resumo: The New York-based artist combines delicate pencil drawings with the nostalgic graphics of the early internet, exploring intimacy and the blurry line between what’s real and what’s artificial. A swallow perches on a…
noticias.trecho: The New York-based artist combines delicate pencil drawings with the nostalgic graphics of the early internet, exploring intimacy and the blurry line between what’s real and what’s artificial. A swallow perches on a white plastic garden chair beside a column of blue folder icons, apparently waiting for a download to finish. A pale sky lifted from a computer desktop frames a bird circled in red under the instruction “Enter the following”, and the answer typed in the box below reads “birds :-)”. In her artworks, Gigi Borgese draws every detail by hand, and the gentle humour really rises to the surface once you know where it all comes from. Growing up in San Jose, California, Gigi describes herself as largely self-taught, having spent much of her life as what she calls “a passive creative”. referencias.trecho: First coming to the attention of Directors Notes at BFI London Flare and then featuring in our Best of Fest list for last year’s BFI London Film Festival where it won the Best Short Film Award, Said Zagha’s tension-soaked Coyotes has continued its success by being nominated for Best British Short Film at the British Independent Film Awards . The thriller follows a Palestinian nurse driving home one night before running into car trouble along an isolated road, where a would-be Good Samaritan offering to assist her proves he’s anything but. It’s a film that has an undercurrent of oppression throughout which reaches a boiling point when a secret is threatened with exposure. referencias.trecho: Founder/director Gints Gutmanis and the Panic design and animation team nudge Yelp’s new illustration style into the motion world with this fresh and friendly campaign film “It Takes a Village”. Gints Gutmanis: This is Yelp’s first animated campaign since its brand identity refresh. It turns the power of community into a miniature neighborhood made of building blocks.   “Everything moves at 12 fps for a handmade, stop-motion feel, and the blocks double as transitions. The characters carry the feelings, and the pets even got cel animation for extra cuteness.”   Everyone has that home project they keep putting off. The real blocker isn’t the project, it’s the doubt: what will it cost, who can I trust, and how long will it take? In this village, the answer comes from neighbors. biblioteca.titulo: Entre el ambientalismo y el documental social: la mirada de Alejandro Fernández Mouján sobre Chaco
biblioteca.resumo: Este artículo se detiene en los primeros films del documentalista argentino Alejandro Fernández Mouján que abordan, en su conjunto, distintas problemáticas de la región de Chaco (Argentina) en un contexto de avance…
biblioteca.trecho: Este artículo se detiene en los primeros films del documentalista argentino Alejandro Fernández Mouján que abordan, en su conjunto, distintas problemáticas de la región de Chaco (Argentina) en un contexto de avance neoliberal. El análisis se detiene en los diálogos que estos films establecen entre sí a partir de la recurrencia de ciertos motivos audiovisuales y del trabajo sobre operaciones de archivo. A la luz de la trayectoria del realizador, este artículo también estudia cómo la búsqueda narrativa en estos films navega entre las formas y las temáticas del cine ambiental, sin alejarse de los lineamientos de la tradición del documental social argentino y latinoamericano.

bolhas.titulo: How many Native people are missing or murdered in California? The state still can’t say
bolhas.resumo: Melanie Henshaw ICT + CalMatters In 2020, California legislators ordered the state Department of Justice to find out how many Native Americans and Alaska Native people in California are missing or have been murdered…
bolhas.trecho: Melanie Henshaw ICT + CalMatters In 2020, California legislators ordered the state Department of Justice to find out how many Native Americans and Alaska Native people in California are missing or have been murdered, and what more the state could do to report and find them. Janet Bill, director of the department’s Office of Native American Affairs and the chairwoman of the Picayune Rancheria of the Chukchansi Indians, told an Assembly budget subcommittee in April that the report was “in the final stages of internal review.” Seven months later, there still is no report. In an unsigned statement sent by email, the Department of Justice said the report is now expected this winter.  The state set aside $5 million in 2021 for the study and for a tribal assistance program meant to help law enforcement agencies and tribal governments navigate overlapping jurisdiction on tribal lands. bolhas.trecho: The Bukhara Biennial has revealed the preliminary artist lineup for its second edition, titled “The Long Welcome,” which is slated to run from September 3 to November 21, 2027. Directed by Thai architect and designer Kulapat Yantrasast, the exhibition will delve into the city’s historic role as a major Silk Road gateway, further drawing on Uzbek hospitality culture, which is rooted in reciprocity.  The biennial will feature a balanced selection of international and homegrown practitioners. The first confirmed cohort includes 13 artists: Anish Kapoor, Koo Jeong A, Sevara Haydarova Donazzan, Susan Philipsz, Nigina Mirzadzhanova, Precious Okoyomon, Ugo Rondinone, Vivian Suter, Joseph Arzoumanov, Oscar Tuazon, Maksim Vardanyan and Daima Rakhmanbekova, Huma Bhabha, and Bethan Laura Wood. bolhas.titulo: Native lawmaker helps Native candidate make history
bolhas.resumo: Amelia Schafer ICT The longest-serving Indigenous woman in the U.S. Congress thinks more Native people should be national lawmakers. So she went on the road to campaign for other Indigenous candidates and met with…
bolhas.trecho: Amelia Schafer ICT The longest-serving Indigenous woman in the U.S. Congress thinks more Native people should be national lawmakers. So she went on the road to campaign for other Indigenous candidates and met with largely untapped voter blocs: Indigenous people. “Native representation in Congress matters,” said Rep. Sharice Davids of Kansas. The Democrat represents the state’s 3rd Congressional District. In Michigan she found success, helping elect Sean McCann, a citizen of the Citizen Potawatomi Nation, as the first Native to represent Michigan in Congress. Rep. Sharice Davids (D-Kans.) speaks to a crowd in Michigan while campaigning alongside now representative-elect Sean McCann (D-Mich.).
